status: Specified locally before any measured program outcomes. Six protocols and their shared source are frozen together before the first run; no results from one study may tune another. Not public preregistration.
uncertainty_scope: Paired percentile bootstrap of 16 seed means, averaging cases and roles within seed. Primary intervals use nominal Bonferroni 99.167% coverage for six predeclared primary comparisons; bootstrap coverage is approximate. All secondary intervals are 95%, exploratory and unadjusted. Neither authored cases nor rounds are independent map-population draws.
fresh_split: Two new behavior rules crossed with two new map templates, parameterized by separate seed streams. Shared across these six simultaneously locked protocols; reuse does not constitute six independently invented generators. After examination these become regression fixtures.
invariants: Archived Rust/Wasm core and Arena.update physical simulation. No weapon, speed, HP, visibility or cooldown changes.
Single-enemy cases retain only the specified live enemy. Inactive array slots preserve bullet IDs and contribute no targeting, collisions, damage, observation or feedback.

Synthetic players receive delayed self state, visible enemies and telegraphs, nearby visible projectiles and public map geometry only. No tactic IDs, policy cells, hidden positions or scripted phase labels.
Terrain context derives only from public wall area: more than 5.5% is dense, otherwise sparse. No player family or direction is supplied to the learner.
Frozen counterparts fork from the exact online boundary, including RNG. Full combats, inputs, choices, observations and reward commits retained.
All valid worlds and outcomes retained; geometry rejection reasons recorded.
No threshold, seed count, generator, reward, training schedule or candidate changes after measurement.
No algorithm installed in the game on the basis of these screens alone.
budget: Equal declared encounter histories within each comparison, with actual simulation steps, decision counts, elapsed time and CPU recorded. This is not an equal-CPU or equal-step claim. Replays and unit-test fights are not additional scored evidence.
limits: Authored tactics and small fixed family sets; no arbitrary-game or opponent-population generalization.
Tactic choices occur once per encounter. This tests between-encounter adaptation, not within-fight tactical replanning.
Only specified host representations/rewards change; the core API is reused without modification.
Negative and insensitive fixtures are retained. A failed screen is not evidence that an entire research direction cannot work.

Lowest damage is a hardness heuristic, not a measurement of future learning value. Probe costs count even when selection is unhelpful. Compare adaptive24 with uniform24 secondarily to isolate selection under matched update counts.
question: Can weakness-directed example selection improve reserved effectiveness within the same total encounter budget?
procedure: Three independent-role original-reward arms: uniform48 (48 training); uniform24 (24 training plus 24 ignored frozen probes); adaptive24 (24 training plus 24 selection probes). Eight cycles each probe three training-only cases from the same checkpoint, choose lowest damage with deterministic ID tie-break, then train three episodes. Frozen probes never change training state. Evaluate all three frozen on four reserved cases, six encounters each direction (12 per case).
primary_endpoint: Adaptive24 minus uniform48 damage averaged across all twelve frozen test fights and four reserved cases.
gate: Primary mean >=3 HP and nominal multiplicity-adjusted lower bound >0; no fresh case mean primary difference below -6 HP. Passing only nominates a follow-up. Additional gate: adaptive24 must not trail uniform24 in fresh mean damage at matched update counts.

demonstration.selection: First seed and first fresh case selected before outcomes; retain unfavorable or equal comparisons.
